new-problem.title: The New Engineering Problem
new-problem.claim: Implementation became abundant; trustworthy judgment did not. The scarce work moved upstream: what to build, how to represent and validate it, not typing the code.
new-problem.more: Generative models did not make software easier to write so much as cheap to write, at a volume no reviewer can keep pace with — so implementation turned abundant while judgment stayed scarce. The bottleneck moved with it, upstream of the keyboard: deciding what to build, representing the system so a fleet can reason over it, validating that the result is faithful, keeping the whole coherent. Accountability does not transfer with the typing — you can delegate the implementation and still own the outcome — so leverage shifts to engineering the conditions under which implementations are produced. That place is the environment, and it becomes the object of the work.

entry_figures.caption: *Where the work moves.* Most of the field tunes the agent and treats the environment as a passive backdrop. The shift this idea names runs the other way: the object of engineering jumps to the governed environment the agent operates inside.

churn.title: Engineering Capital — Churn vs. Compounding
churn.claim: One environment, two fates. Ungoverned, effort dissipates as churn — rediscovering, undoing, reconciling. Governed and converting, it accrues as engineering capital: the same effort compounds.
churn.more: Scale creates a reasoning problem before it creates anything else. An agent fleet is cheap and fast, so it scales — up to the context window. Once the work a change requires exceeds what a single context can hold, the fleet stops advancing the system and starts churning: it re-derives architecture it already worked out, re-opens settled questions, and confidently undoes yesterday's fix. That is churn, effort re-spent rather than banked. The same environment has a positive sign: govern each recurring failure and convert it, and the effort banks as engineering capital that lowers the cost of every later change. The fork is what the whole method decides; Part 6 cashes the compounding half.

entry_figures.caption: *The compounding pole.* Convert a recurring failure into a durable control and it joins the substrate later work stands on. The environment's engineering capital grows one retired failure at a time, so the same effort that would have dissipated as churn instead accrues.

modeling-thesis.title: Documentation, taken to its limit, is a structured model
modeling-thesis.claim: A context-bounded agent can't hold the whole system. Externalize what it must know into structured, drift-checked models, purposeful compression, and the reasoning fits the window.
modeling-thesis.more: A foundation model reasons through a bounded context and rebuilds its picture of the system on every task; a real change's reasoning state outruns that working memory, so it is compressed and reconstructed, and every lossy round trip degrades the reasoning it stands in for. A model answers that chain at its source. It is *purposeful compression* — keep the subsystem, interface, invariant, and workflow relationships engineering questions actually need, discard the rest — so each reconstruction restores more of what mattered and the reasoning horizon stretches. Models used to die because keeping them current was somebody's unpaid job; agents now do it for cents, and a drifted model fails the build where a drifted prose doc only lies quietly. Modeling is representation, not authority: a model helps a reasoner think, but nothing forces the code to obey it until Alignment gives it teeth — and richer models simply widen the surface that authority can later reach.

entry_figures.caption: *The reasoning horizon, and what a model does to it.* Reasoning state grows with a task's length; once it outruns working memory it must be compacted. Reason through a model and each compaction loses less, so the horizon stretches and the branch reaches progress instead of churn.

alignment-thesis.title: Give intent authority: constrain, sense, validate, gate
alignment-thesis.claim: Give intent authority over the fleet: constrain the wrong move away, then sense evidence, validate it, and gate what may advance — sensor produces, validator judges.
alignment-thesis.more: A model by itself has no authority — it helps an engineer think and an agent navigate, but nothing forces the code to obey it. Alignment changes that: once intent is explicit enough to check, the environment can enforce it through four mechanism roles. A **constraint** removes the wrong move from the action space, so the failing state is never built. A **sensor** observes the work and *produces evidence* — a log, a trace, a scan of what the code actually did; it does not judge. A **validator** turns that evidence into a judgment against the obligation. A **gate** supplies the consequence, admitting or refusing the change at the door. Prefer the constraint where you can build one; where prevention cannot reach, the sensor–validator–gate chain holds the rest. Alignment can act directly, wherever a property is already legible: a constraint the compiler enforces needs no model at all. What none of the four can reach stays a human's job, named honestly rather than hidden.

convert-failures.title: Convert recurring failures into controls
convert-failures.claim: Velocity surfaces the failures you could not foresee. Convert each recurring one into a mechanism, pushed as far toward hard enforcement as it will go.
convert-failures.more: You cannot foresee every failure a fast fleet will find; velocity is what surfaces them. The practice is to let velocity expose a recurring failure, then diagnose what the environment lacked and convert it — the fix repairs this instance, the conversion changes the environment. The conversion lands wherever the gap is: a missing model, a stated invariant, a sensor, a stronger validator, or new authority — not reflexively another gate. Whatever the branch, the output is the same in kind: durable structure future work inherits, which is **engineering capital**. Two loops reinforce: a knowledge loop turns intent into models into machine-checkable obligations, and a governance loop turns failures into authority into durable controls. Capital is not a ledger that only grows — it forms, is maintained, **depreciates** as the system it guarded moves on, and is retired when its carrying cost outruns its return. So mature adaptation reconciles and retires as well as adds.

entry_figures.caption: *The hardening loop.* A recurring failure is caught, then converted into a mechanism and pushed toward the hardest enforcement it admits, so the class cannot return. The control substrate grows one retired failure at a time.

governance-centric.title: The Engineered Environment
governance-centric.claim: Engineer the environment, not the agent. Encode each obligation as a mechanism the ground enforces, so quality becomes a property of where agents act.
governance-centric.more: This is the argument's payoff and its largest claim: the thing to engineer is not the agent, it is the environment in which the agent is allowed to act. Velocity-centric hands work around a ring of job titles and leaves quality implicit; oversight-centric parks a human beside each change, and attention does not scale with the fleet. Governance-centric pays attention per class of failure instead — once, when you build the mechanism that retires it — so quality stops being a promise in the output or a property of a reviewer's vigilance and becomes a property of the ground agents stand on. It is the one move the industrial systems studied here do not make: each engineers an agent, a runtime, or a policy engine; MAGE engineers the governed environment those operate inside, and the rest of the method falls out of that one choice.

seat-moves.title: The lifecycle stays, but now agents sit in the developer's seat
seat-moves.claim: SDLC becomes SELC: one seat reassigned, the lifecycle otherwise intact. The fleet writes the code; the engineer keeps the seats that were always the engineering.
seat-moves.more: The engineer flanks the fleet: models carry intent in on one side, judgment meets the output on the other. The seats the human keeps — requirements, specification, design, validation — were always the consequential ones; now they are the job. Review itself moves with the weight: away from inspecting each change and toward mechanism design, catching a class of failure once rather than every instance by eye.

independent-convergence.title: Independent Convergence
independent-convergence.claim: Six industrial systems, engineered independently, land on one set of principles. None generalizes the whole theory, yet each instantiates a distinct arm — convergence, not derivation.
independent-convergence.more: One system, however deeply studied, could always be the special case that flatters its own method. The test that carries weight is whether the constructs hold where no one had heard of the method — so the theory was read against six industrial systems built for entirely different reasons. Each leans hard on one arm and barely touches the others; read any one alone and you would reconstruct a fragment. Their independent arrival at the same regions is corroboration, not derivation, and it reads them as implementations of one framework rather than six unrelated tools.

research-agenda.title: The Research Agenda
research-agenda.claim: Three open frontiers: how far judgment can migrate into deterministic machinery, how to census a governed environment's coverage and gaps, and what stronger models unlock.
research-agenda.more: These frontiers are not loose ends; they are where the method turns testable. Each names something you could measure against real systems rather than assert — how far an obligation can be pushed toward proof, what a governed environment's coverage actually is, and what the next tier of models makes cheap enough to retire by hand. The last is the model floor: a stronger environment makes cheaper models viable, so the sharp question becomes whether you can swap models without quality collapse.

entry_figures.caption: *The census frontier, drawn.* Match obligations against the mechanisms that meet them and three counts fall out — governed, under-governed, and governance debt — so an environment's coverage becomes something you measure rather than assert.

gateway.title: The models are the interface; the map is kept equal to the territory
gateway.claim: Two spines of models over one method trunk govern this very repo; the catalogue's mechanisms hold them true.
gateway.more: The models are the interface a context-bounded fleet operates a context-exceeding codebase through. Browse the mechanisms by the model they govern.

core_question.question: How do we safely grant autonomy to commodity intelligence?
core_question.software_specialization: When implementation becomes cheap enough that agents can build almost anything you can describe, what must the surrounding engineering environment do so they can act autonomously without making the system untrustworthy?

through_line.text: How do we safely grant autonomy to commodity intelligence?
Make intent explicit in models the fleet reasons through, and make the environment enforce the obligations that matter.
When autonomy exposes a new failure class, convert the lesson into durable structure so the next agent inherits a safer, more capable world.
